how_it_wins:
Your commander never has to leave the command zone, and that is the best news in the deck. Eminence reads “Whenever you cast another Vampire spell, if Edgar is in the command zone or on the battlefield, create a 1/1 black Vampire creature token” — free, untaxed, from turn one. So every cheap Vampire you cast is two bodies before it does anything else. Put Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Glory Dominus or Elspeth, Storm Slayer underneath it and one trigger makes four: stack 002 verifies the arithmetic, and a multiplier or extra token-maker is drawn in 79.0% of simulated games at a mean turn of 2.68.

Then comes the layer that makes width lethal against three seats at once. Purphoros, God of the Forge, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call each turn a creature entering the battlefield into damage to EACH opponent — no attack step, no blockers, no evasion needed. Stack 008 counts it exactly: one two-mana Vampire through two doublers is five entries and five Purphoros triggers, 10 damage to every opponent. That conversion layer is drawn in 43.2% of games at a mean turn of 3.45, and it arrives with a multiplier alongside it in 33.4%.

Combat is your second kill and it assembles faster than anything else you own — a Vampire lord or anthem shows up in 82.9% of games at a mean turn of 2.58. Stack 003 prices what that buys: seven attacking Vampires under Sanctum Seeker with Bloodletter of Aclazotz out drain each opponent for 14 at declare-attackers, before a single blocker exists. Edgar is the pivot rather than the opener — median cast turn 6, and his attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control the turn he swings. Here is the trap: waiting for him. The token board is already a clock, and the damage triggers do not care whether anything survives to combat.

You also hold a deterministic kill, and you should hold it lightly. Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or with Sanguine Bond is a zero-mana table-kill, both verified (stacks 004 and 006) — and you draw a complete pair in 4.8% of games, 24.0% counting all three unrestricted tutors as wildcards. That is a lottery ticket you happen to be holding, not a plan, and every one of those cards pays rent as a Vampire body or a drain on the turns the loop never happens. Race with the tokens, present the loop only when the window is open, and never hold back a board to protect a pairing that shows up one game in twenty.

combo_lines.002: Begin with CR 616.1, because it is the clause that makes this deck's arithmetic safe: when two replacement effects want the same event, the affected player “chooses one to apply.” Anointed Procession and Mondrak, Glory Dominus both want your single eminence token, and CR 614.5 gives each exactly one bite at it. The plain holding: one token becomes two becomes four, and the order you pick does not change the answer. Two more findings ride along — eminence functions from the command zone because it says which zones it works in (CR 113.6b), and the tokens are created rather than cast, so eminence does not fire again for them.
combo_lines.003: The controlling text is Bloodletter of Aclazotz: “If an opponent would lose life during your turn, they lose twice that much life instead.” Note the word instead — CR 614.1a makes it a replacement effect, and CR 614.5 gives it one application per loss event, not one per turn. Sanctum Seeker triggers once for each attacking Vampire, so seven attackers are seven separate events, each doubled from 1 to 2. The holding you can carry to a table: 14 out of every opponent at declare-attackers, before blockers exist — and your own gain of 1 per trigger is never doubled, because Bloodletter speaks only to an opponent's loss.
combo_lines.004: One parenthesis decides this case. Bloodthirsty Conqueror reads “Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life. (Damage causes loss of life.)”, and CR 207.2a makes that italic clause reminder text — a summary of a rule, not a requirement that the loss be damage. Vito's targeted life loss therefore feeds it, and the handshake closes. The holding: a deterministic table-kill for zero mana, retargetable every iteration because CR 115.1d picks targets fresh as each trigger goes on the stack, and shortcut-legal under CR 732.1b so you never have to count it out loud. The cost is on the record too — both halves are creatures, and every iteration passes priority to a table that may hold instant-speed removal.
combo_lines.006: Sanguine Bond's trigger is word-for-word Vito's: “Whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life.” Everything stack 004 settled about the Conqueror half carries over unchanged, so what is worth naming here is the difference in exposure. Bond is an enchantment, which means this pairing offers exactly one creature to answer instead of two. The holding: the same zero-mana deterministic table-kill with one fewer target — and the chain survives a mid-loop death, because the killing loss triggers Conqueror before state-based actions (CR 704.5a) remove the player.
combo_lines.007: Read this one as the warning label it is. Throne of the God-Pharaoh drains each opponent for the number of tapped creatures you control at the beginning of your end step; the ending phase is still your turn, so Bloodletter doubles each opponent's loss separately under CR 614.1a. Seven tapped creatures is 14 out of each seat, and an untapped Bloodletter that stayed home is not one of the seven. Now the honest holding, stated as the record states it: this is verified reach and a refuted table-kill. An opponent at 15 survives at exactly 1, CR 104.2a's win condition is not met, and play continues in your end step.
combo_lines.008: The question of law is a counting question, and CR 603.2c answers it: an ability “can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.” Four tokens entering simultaneously is one event containing four occurrences, not one entry. So Purphoros triggers four times, then a fifth time when the spell's own body resolves and enters. The holding: five triggers at 2 damage each is 10 to every opponent from a single two-mana Vampire cast — and Purphoros being a noncreature enchantment at low devotion changes none of it.

card_roles.Edgar Markov: The engine that never needs to be cast: eminence mints a 1/1 black Vampire for every other Vampire spell you cast, from the command zone, all game, for nothing. When he does land (goldfish median turn 6), cast him as the alpha-strike pivot — first strike and haste mean he leads the swing the turn he arrives, and his attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control.
card_roles.Anointed Procession: Doubler one, and the cheapest way to make every eminence trigger worth twice as much. Stack 002 verifies that it and Mondrak apply once each to the same token event, in either order, for four tokens off one trigger.
card_roles.Mondrak, Glory Dominus: Doubler two, on a 4/4 body that can protect itself by sacrificing two other permanents for an indestructible counter — and eminence tokens are exactly the permanents you can spare. It is a Phyrexian Horror, not a Vampire, so casting it makes no token of its own.
card_roles.Elspeth, Storm Slayer: Doubler three, with a static ability that needs no combat and a +1 that makes a Soldier every turn to feed it. Her 0 puts a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control and gives them flying until your next turn, which turns a token board into an evasive one for a turn.
card_roles.Purphoros, God of the Forge: The heaviest converter in the deck: 2 damage to each opponent for every other creature you control entering the battlefield. Stack 008 measures the ceiling at 10 damage to every opponent off one two-mana Vampire cast — and because devotion to red usually keeps him a noncreature, he is an indestructible enchantment a creature sweeper cannot touch.
card_roles.Impact Tremors: The same conversion for two mana: 1 damage to each opponent every time a creature you control enters. It is an enchantment, so it survives everything aimed at your board and keeps charging rent while you rebuild.
card_roles.Warleader's Call: Conversion and combat in one card — every creature you control gets +1/+1, and every creature entering deals 1 damage to each opponent. In a deck with 29 creature copies and a token engine, that anthem is quietly the largest single buff you can play.
card_roles.Charismatic Conqueror: A tax that makes tokens on other people’s turns: whenever an artifact or creature an opponent controls enters untapped, they either tap it themselves or hand you a 1/1 white lifelink Vampire. Against three seats both branches are good for you, and it is a two-mana Vampire, so casting it is already two bodies.
card_roles.Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fo: A one-mana lifelink Vampire that transforms the first time you attack with three or more creatures — a threshold this deck crosses routinely. The back face is a white source that makes another lifelink Vampire for {2}{W}, so it is a land that keeps feeding the entry triggers.
card_roles.Mavren Fein, Dusk Apostle: Every attack with one or more nontoken Vampires makes a 1/1 white lifelink Vampire — a token per combat, doubled by any doubler, and another entry for the damage payoffs.
card_roles.Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage: A repeatable 2/2 flying Vampire every turn with no mana required, which is the shape token doublers like best. Once you control five Vampires, flip it for {B} and the whole team gets +2/+2.
card_roles.Ocelot Pride: A one-mana first-strike lifelink body that pays off the deck's constant incidental lifegain: gain any life and it makes a Cat at your end step. With the city's blessing it copies every token that entered this turn, which on a doubled eminence turn is a second wave.
card_roles.Preacher of the Schism: Deathtouch on a three-mana Vampire, plus a choice the table cannot make comfortable: attack the player with the most life and you get a 1/1 lifelink Vampire; attack while you have the most life and you draw.
card_roles.Elenda, the Dusk Rose: A lifelink Vampire that grows on every other creature's death and cashes out into that many 1/1 white lifelink Vampires when she dies — a token wave that a sweeper triggers rather than prevents, and one your doublers double.
card_roles.Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet: Turns opponents' removal into a punishment: their nontoken creatures are exiled instead of dying and you get a 2/2 Zombie each time. Its sacrifice ability gives you a place to put spare tokens when Kalitas needs to be bigger.
card_roles.Legion Lieutenant: Two mana, other Vampires get +1/+1. In a deck averaging 4.12 bodies by turn six, that anthem is paid many times over — and it is a Vampire spell, so it brings its own token.
card_roles.Stromkirk Captain: The lord that changes combat math rather than just size: other Vampires get +1/+1 and first strike, which makes a wide board of small tokens miserable to block.
card_roles.Captivating Vampire: A +1/+1 lord with a theft button attached — tap five untapped Vampires to steal any creature permanently and make it a Vampire. Untapped tokens are the cost, so a doubled eminence turn pays for it.
card_roles.Patchwork Banner: Name Vampire and it is a colourless lord that also taps for any colour — one of the four rocks lifting black on-curve from 63.9% to 71.8%. A buff and a source in one card is the correct shape for a curve this cheap.
card_roles.Vanquisher's Banner: The expensive lord, bought for the draw clause: name Vampire and every Vampire spell you cast replaces itself. Five mana is real in this curve, so cast it on a turn you can still deploy.
card_roles.Shared Animosity: The combat multiplier, and it scales with exactly what the deck produces — each attacker gets +1/+0 for every other attacking creature sharing its type. Eight attacking Vampires is +7/+0 each.
card_roles.Abzan Falconer: Flying for every creature you control carrying a +1/+1 counter, which this deck distributes freely through Edgar's attack trigger, Vampire Socialite, Cordial Vampire and Elspeth. It is a Human Soldier, so it makes no eminence token — it is here for evasion, not width.
card_roles.Vampire Socialite: Menace plus a counter engine keyed to something you cause constantly: while an opponent has lost life this turn, every other Vampire enters with an extra +1/+1 counter. Stack 002 confirms the tokens get it too, which turns a doubled eminence trigger into four 2/2s.
card_roles.Cordial Vampire: Every creature death anywhere puts a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control — a two-mana card that turns a board stall or a sweeper into permanent size across your whole team.
card_roles.Drana, Liberator of Malakir: Flying and first strike for three, and her combat damage puts a +1/+1 counter on every attacking creature you control. First strike means the counters land before regular damage, so the rest of the swing hits bigger.
card_roles.Knight of the Ebon Legion: A one-drop that never stops scaling: {2}{B} makes it a 4/4 deathtouch, and it grows permanently at your end step whenever a player lost 4 or more life this turn — a condition the entry-damage payoffs satisfy on their own.
card_roles.Cover of Darkness: Name Vampire and the swarm gains fear, blockable only by artifact or black creatures. This is the card that unsticks a board stall when the arithmetic already favours you.
card_roles.Vampire of the Dire Moon: One mana, deathtouch and lifelink. It blanks an attacker all game, banks an eminence token on the way in, and its lifelink triggers anything keyed to your life gain.
card_roles.Bloodletter of Aclazotz: The doubler on the other axis: every opponent's life loss during your turn is doubled. Stack 003 verifies it applies per loss event, not per turn — seven Sanctum Seeker triggers become 14 out of each seat.
card_roles.Sanctum Seeker: Each attacking Vampire costs every opponent 1 life and gains you 1 — a drain that fires at declare-attackers and cannot be blocked away. Stack 003 verifies seven attackers under Bloodletter as 14 out of each opponent before blockers.
card_roles.Throne of the God-Pharaoh: Two mana that converts a tapped-out attack into a second drain at your end step, equal to the number of tapped creatures you control. Stack 007 verifies the reach and bounds it honestly: seven tapped creatures under Bloodletter is 14 per opponent, which is not lethal by default.
card_roles.Bloodthirsty Conqueror: A 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire that gains you life whenever any opponent loses it — which the entry triggers, Sanctum Seeker attacks and Throne end steps all cause anyway. With Vito or Sanguine Bond it is a verified zero-mana table-kill (stacks 004 and 006); without either, it is still one of the best blockers you can present.
card_roles.Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose: Every point of life you gain becomes targeted life loss, on a three-mana Vampire body that pays rent as an eminence trigger and a lord target. Stack 004 verifies the loop with Bloodthirsty Conqueror; its {3}{B}{B} ability gives the whole team lifelink for one drain-everything combat.
card_roles.Sanguine Bond: Vito's trigger word for word, on an enchantment — which is the point, because it gives the loop a half no creature removal can answer. Stack 006 verifies the kill with Bloodthirsty Conqueror at zero mana and one exposed creature instead of two.
card_roles.Twilight Prophet: A four-mana flier that, once you control ten permanents, drains every opponent for a card's mana value each upkeep and refills your hand with it. A wide token board reaches ten permanents without trying.
card_roles.Bontu's Monument: Discounts every black creature spell by {1} and drains each opponent for 1 on every creature cast. Two effects the deck uses on nearly every turn, on an artifact nobody bothers to remove.
card_roles.Sorin, Imperious Bloodlord: Three modes the deck wants: deathtouch and lifelink with a counter on a Vampire, a Vampire sacrificed for 3 damage anywhere plus 3 life, or a Vampire put straight onto the battlefield from hand. That last mode cheats past the curve and still triggers your entry payoffs.
card_roles.Henrika Domnathi // Henrika, Infernal Se: A flier that offers a different mode each combat — an edict at the table, a card, or a transform into a 3/3 flying deathtouch lifelink threat that pumps your evasive creatures. Three uses out of one four-mana Vampire.
card_roles.Strefan, Maurer Progenitor: A flier that turns a turn in which people lost life into Blood tokens — which, in this deck, is most turns. Sacrifice two on an attack to put a Vampire from hand onto the battlefield tapped, attacking and indestructible.
card_roles.Caretaker's Talent: Draws a card the first time tokens enter each turn, which is a card on nearly every turn you cast a Vampire. Level 2 copies a token you control; level 3 gives every creature token +2/+2 and turns the swarm into a real combat force.
card_roles.Welcoming Vampire: A flier that draws a card the first time other small creatures enter each turn — and a doubled eminence trigger is exactly that. Board-gated draw is the right kind here, because a board is what this deck has.
card_roles.Night's Whisper: Two cards for two mana and two life. The cheapest way to convert a spare early turn into fuel, and life is a resource this deck regenerates through lifelink.
card_roles.Minas Tirith: A white source that draws a card for {1}{W} on any turn you attacked with two or more creatures — a condition this board meets by default. It enters untapped whenever you control a legendary creature.
card_roles.Castle Locthwain: A black source with a refill button attached: {1}{B}{B} to draw at the cost of life equal to your hand size, which is cheapest exactly when you are empty and need it most.
card_roles.Demonic Tutor: Any card, no restriction, two mana. Point it at the conversion layer when you have the board, or at the missing loop half when the table is tapped out.
card_roles.Vampiric Tutor: Instant-speed access to any card at the cost of your draw step — the right way to hold up a threat and a decision at once. Cast it on the turn before you need the card, not two turns early.
card_roles.Diabolic Intent: A tutor whose additional cost is a creature you were going to make anyway. Sacrificing a spare eminence token is close to free, which makes this the cheapest of the three in real terms.
card_roles.Teferi's Protection: The best answer in the deck to a sweeper, a lethal swing and a loop-breaking removal spell at once: everything you control phases out and your life total cannot change until your next turn.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free while you control a commander, and board-wide indestructible is the right shape when the thing being answered is a wrath. Note the tension — free means Edgar on the battlefield, and the eminence plan is happy to leave him home.
card_roles.Akroma's Will: The protection spell that also ends games: flying, vigilance and double strike, or lifelink, indestructible and protection from each colour — and with a commander out, both. On a wide board either half is a swing of many points.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Three answers on one card: 4 damage to a player, indestructible for every permanent you control, or double strike for a single attacker. The middle mode is the one you hold up.
card_roles.Deflecting Swat: Free while you control a commander, and it redirects the removal spell or the trigger aimed at the piece you cannot afford to lose. Change targets, do not counter — it works on abilities too.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for one mana of equip. On Edgar it turns the pivot turn into a same-turn attack; on a loop half it makes targeted removal look elsewhere.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: The cleanest one-mana answer in the format. Hold it for the creature that actually threatens you, not the first one that resolves.
card_roles.Path to Exile: The second one-mana exile. The basic land you hand over matters far less than the threat that stops existing.
card_roles.Despark: Two mana, exile any permanent with mana value 4 or greater — the deck's answer to the enchantment, artifact or planeswalker that a creature removal spell cannot touch.
card_roles.Winds of Abandon: A spot exile early and a one-sided wrath late: overload for {4}{W}{W} and every creature you do not control leaves, while your board stays whole and swings.
card_roles.Olivia's Wrath: A sweeper that reads as one-sided here — every non-Vampire creature shrinks by the number of Vampires you control, and the token swarm makes that number large.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: The answer to a board yours cannot beat, paid in life rather than mana. It hits your creatures too, so cast it as a reset when you can rebuild off eminence, not as a tempo play.
card_roles.Cemetery Gatekeeper: A two-mana first-striking Vampire that exiles a card from a graveyard on arrival and then taxes every player who plays a land or casts a spell sharing that card's type for 2 damage. Choose the exile with the table's decks in mind — it is a repeatable clock nobody removes early.
card_roles.Viscera Seer: The deck's one true sacrifice outlet, on a one-mana Vampire that banks its own eminence token. It turns spare tokens into card selection, gives Elenda a way to cash out on your terms, and feeds Mondrak's indestructible-counter cost.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two extra mana from turn one. It buys speed rather than colour, which in this deck means double-spelling Vampires a turn earlier.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any colour in Edgar's identity for two mana — one of the four sources lifting black on-curve from 63.9% to 71.8%.
card_roles.Talisman of Indulgence: Black or red for a point of life, on the two-mana rung where this deck most wants to be casting Vampires anyway.
card_roles.Herald's Horn: Name Vampire and every creature spell costs {1} less, plus a free look at the top of your library each upkeep for another one. On a curve of 9 one-drops and 17 two-drops, that rebate is close to a permanent extra mana.
card_roles.Ancient Tomb: Two colourless for 2 damage. A turn-one Tomb into a two-drop Vampire is one of the fastest openings the deck has, and the life is a currency you regain through lifelink.
card_roles.Mana Confluence: Any colour, one life a time. In a base whose black leg is the tight one, this is the land that always says yes.
card_roles.Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth: Every land is a Swamp — the single best patch for a manabase carrying 53.4% of its pips in black on 41.5% of its sources. Your white and red lands start paying black under it.
card_roles.Reflecting Pool: Any colour a land you control could produce. It is only as good as the rest of the base, and this base is three-colour by turn three.
card_roles.Savai Triome: All three colours on one land, at the cost of always entering tapped — one of only three that do so unconditionally. Cycle it for {3} once the mana is settled.
card_roles.Nomad Outpost: The other unconditional tapland, and the price is worth paying on a turn you were not casting anything anyway.
card_roles.Blood Crypt: Black and red untapped for 2 life, or tapped for free. Pay the life on turns you have a play; take the tap when you do not.
card_roles.Godless Shrine: Black and white untapped for 2 life — the two colours you most want on turns one and two.
card_roles.Sacred Foundry: Red and white for 2 life. The red half matters for exactly three cards in the deck, so take it tapped more often than you think.
card_roles.Caves of Koilos: Colourless for free, black or white for a point of damage. A painland is at its best on the early turns this curve lives in.
card_roles.Battlefield Forge: Colourless for free, red or white for a point. It untaps into Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call.
card_roles.Sulfurous Springs: Colourless for free, black or red for a point — the untapped source that casts a turn-one one-drop and a turn-two two-drop.
card_roles.Silent Clearing: Black or white for a life, and it cashes itself in for a card late when you have lands to spare.
card_roles.Sunbaked Canyon: Red or white for a life, with the same draw-a-card exit once the land drops stop mattering.
card_roles.Bleachbone Verge: Black for free, white once you control a Plains or a Swamp — an untapped dual on the turns that decide the game.
card_roles.Blazemire Verge: Black for free, red once you control a Swamp or a Mountain. The red half is a luxury; the black half is the point.
card_roles.Concealed Courtyard: Black or white, untapped while you control two or fewer other lands — exactly the window a curve of 9 one-drops cares about.
card_roles.Shattered Sanctum: Black or white, untapped once you control two or more other lands. The complement to the fastland, covering the later turns.
card_roles.Haunted Ridge: Black or red, untapped from your third land onward.
card_roles.Sundown Pass: Red or white, untapped from your third land onward.
card_roles.Luxury Suite: Black or red, untapped whenever you have two or more opponents — which in Commander is nearly always.
card_roles.Vault of Champions: Black or white on the same two-opponent condition, and black-white is the pairing this deck opens on.
card_roles.Spectator Seating: Red or white on the same condition. The least urgent of the three, because red is the lightest colour load at 15.1% of pips.
card_roles.Cori Mountain Monastery: A red source with an impulse-draw button for {3}{R} — a mana sink for the turns you have drawn out.
card_roles.Takenuma, Abandoned Mire: A black source that channels away to return a creature from the graveyard, and it costs {1} less for each legendary creature you control — of which this deck has plenty.
card_roles.Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid: An adventure land: cast Reactor Raid from hand to sacrifice an artifact or creature and draw two — spare eminence tokens are the intended fuel — then play the land itself later from exile. It is one of only three lands here that enter tapped unconditionally.
card_roles.Arid Mesa: Fetches a Mountain or Plains dual — in practice Sacred Foundry or the untapped white lands — for a life.
card_roles.Bloodstained Mire: Fetches a Swamp or Mountain dual for a life. Point it at Blood Crypt when you need both halves.
card_roles.Marsh Flats: Fetches a Plains or Swamp dual for a life — the fetch that finds the black-white lands this curve opens on.
card_roles.Prismatic Vista: Fetches any basic for a life. With five basics in the deck it is the flexible one, and it thins toward the colour the turn actually needs.
card_roles.Swamp: Four copies, the fetchable and Urborg-independent backbone of a base carrying 39 black pips across 29 cards.
card_roles.Plains: The lone white basic — the Prismatic Vista target and the reason a fetched Plains is ever an option.

mulligan:
Keep hands that do something on turn two. That is the whole test, and this deck passes it easily — 81.7% of first sevens clear the goldfish's own keep rule and mean mulligans run 0.214, so you are not fighting your own list for a hand. Concretely: two to four lands plus at least two Vampires you can cast by turn three. There are 9 one-drops and 17 two-drops to find, and each of those casts is a body and an eminence token.

The seductive trap is the all-payoff keep. Sanguine Bond, Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Vanquisher's Banner in the same seven is a hand that does nothing until turn five and then asks the table's permission. Ship it. Ship zero- and one-land hands, ship six-land hands, and ship anything whose cheapest spell costs four.

Do not mulligan looking for a specific card, including the ones you most want. A lord or anthem is drawn in 82.9% of games at a mean turn of 2.58 and a multiplier in 79.0% at 2.68 — the payoffs find you. Purphoros, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call are the thinner leg at 43.2%, and the right response to that is to keep a curve that can use one the moment it shows up, not to dig for it at six cards.

Two details that decide close keeps. Sixteen of the 37 lands can enter tapped, though only Nomad Outpost, Savai Triome and Midgar, City of Mako do it unconditionally — so a two-land keep wants at least one source that comes in untapped for the one-drop start. And never keep a hand for Edgar: his median cast is turn 6, eminence works from the command zone the whole time, and a seven built around a six-drop is a seven built around your slowest card. Herald's Horn, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet or Talisman of Indulgence turn a marginal keep into a good one; ramp or fixing lands in 68.4% of games at a mean turn of 2.95.
upgrades:
Price the Short List against one question: how often does a token entering the battlefield cost the table life? Right now the answer is 43.2% of games, 34.1% of them by turn six — which means roughly two games in three reach turn six with the conversion layer still in the library. Compare that to the width the deck manufactures anyway: a multiplier or extra token-maker at 79.0% and a lord or anthem at 82.9%, both arriving before turn three on average. The bodies are not the constraint. The thing that turns bodies into damage is.

Two axes read thin on the audit and one of them is real. Ramp sits at 7 copies against a 10-12 band, and the curve it is feeding has a modal mana value of 3 in a deck that wants two spells a turn. Card advantage counts 4 against a floor of 10, but the audit itself flags six more draw functions on cards it classifies elsewhere — Castle Locthwain, Henrika Domnathi, Midgar, Minas Tirith, Preacher of the Schism, Savai Triome — so treat that number as a floor, not a diagnosis. Interaction runs the other way at 12 copies against an aggro template's 5 or 6, and those six extra slots are the budget the width plan is not spending.

One number to stop worrying about: the bracket. The floor is 4 and it is set by four Game Changers — Ancient Tomb, Demonic Tutor, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor — independently of any combo content. So nothing on this list moves the deck's power tier, and nothing on it should be chosen to. Every entry below is bought for a rate: another payoff that converts entries to damage, another source of entries, or the mana to deploy two of them in a turn. That is the purchase, and the currency is the interaction slots the audit says you are over on.
mana_base:
Thirty-seven lands across 34 entries, and the figure to sit with first is 16 — the number that can enter tapped. That is 43% of the base against the one-in-three budget the deck builder allows itself, which sounds worse than it plays: only three of them (Nomad Outpost, Savai Triome, Midgar, City of Mako) enter tapped unconditionally. The rest are shocks, verges, checks and fastlands that come in untapped when you meet their condition. Land drops hit 99.8% on turn two and 92.1% on turn three, with mean available mana of 2.149 and 3.176 on those turns.

The interesting disagreement is between pips and sources, and it is entirely black. Black carries 53.4% of the deck's pips on 41.5% of its sources — 39 pips across 29 cards, up to three at a time, standing on 22 land sources. Red is the mirror image at 15.1% of pips on 26.4% of sources, and white is the one colour where the two agree, 31.5% against 32.1%. You are, in other words, best supported in the colour you need least.

On-curve probability prices that skew exactly. From lands alone, white arrives 83.1% of the time and red 76.2%; black arrives 63.9%. Your tightest leg is your heaviest colour, and that is the whole shape of this manabase in one number.

The rocks buy a real slice of it back. Arcane Signet, Patchwork Banner, Talisman of Indulgence and the back face of Legion's Landing take black from 22 sources to 25 and 63.9% to 71.8%, white to 88.1%, red to 83.1%. Sol Ring adds speed, not colour. Patchwork Banner is the standout of the group because it is a lord that taps for any colour, and the two cost reducers — Herald's Horn and Bontu's Monument — lower the bill rather than raising the sources, which is the same thing on a curve this cheap. Nothing in the deck produces restricted mana, so every source can pay for an activated ability.

About the 90% yardstick: it asks for 36 black sources against 22 red and 22 white. Thirty-six black sources in a 37-land deck is arithmetic that does not exist, and the audit says so itself — a yardstick, not a possibility. So read the gap as posture rather than as a defect. Sequence black first, keep the untapped black-white lands for one-drop starts, and let Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth do its trick: with it out, every land you control is a Swamp and the whole base taps for the colour the audit flags.
threat_assessment:
The table reads Edgar Markov at seat assignment, and you should let it. Eminence works from the command zone, so a Vampire cast on turn two is a body whether or not you ever pay six mana for him. The goldfish measures 0.91 bodies by turn two, 1.75 by turn three and 4.12 by turn six. "I haven't done anything yet" is not a sentence available to you.

So stop spending your deflection budget on anonymity. It cannot buy that (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection). What it can buy is the order you deploy three specific cards in, and that ordering is worth more than any bluff you could tell.

Here is the flip point, and it is exact. You go from a creature deck to the archenemy the first time a token entering deals damage at all three seats. Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros each do that. Before that trigger you are a fair board. After it, everyone is on your clock and no combat step is required.

The flip is measured, not felt. A token-to-damage payoff is drawn in 43.2% of games at a mean turn of 3.45. Paired with a multiplier, 33.4%, mean turn 4.66. Stack 008 verifies the ceiling: with Anointed Procession and Mondrak, Glory Dominus down, one two-mana Vampire is five Purphoros triggers and 10 damage to each opponent.

So sequence payoffs early and multipliers late. Impact Tremors on turn two with one body is one damage and reads as durdle; nobody spends removal on it. Anointed Procession is three mana that visibly does nothing. Elspeth, Storm Slayer is a five-mana planeswalker and gets attacked on sight, so she is the last piece down, never the first.

Now the good news, and say it out loud at the table. A creature sweeper is the wrong answer to you. Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Caretaker's Talent, Patchwork Banner, Legion's Landing and Elspeth all live through one. Purphoros is indestructible, and while your devotion to red is under five he is not even a creature.

Eminence rebuilds at one token per Vampire cast, with no card spent and no commander tax. That makes the wrath in someone's hand a bad trade against you and a fine one against the seat to your left. Pointing that out is free, and it is true, which is the only kind of table talk that keeps working.

Your actual exposure is the enchantment layer. Track which seat holds broad exile or artifact-and-enchantment removal, and treat that player as the one who can turn the machine off.

Bloodthirsty Conqueror is the card to stay quiet about, and the reason is not that it wins. It is that it wins so rarely. The pairing with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond is a verified deterministic table-kill (stacks 004 and 006), and it is drawn in 4.8% of games, 2.6% by turn six, 24.0% counting the three tutors as wildcards. That is a lottery ticket riding along with a real plan. Never hold the board back to protect it.

Deploy that package by how each card looks. Vito is a three-mana Vampire and a lord target, so cast it on curve and it tells nobody anything. Conqueror is a 5/5 flying deathtouch body that pays full rent, so cast it as a body whenever you do not hold the other half. Sanguine Bond is five mana with no body and no creature type, and it is the one card in the deck that announces itself.

Stacks 004 and 006 both name the honest cost: instant-speed creature removal in any iteration's priority window breaks the loop. Count the table's open mana before you present it (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). If a seat has two untapped and a reputation for holding, cast the enchantment half and pass.

Then take the label, on the turn the arithmetic is already there. Two boards qualify. A payoff plus a multiplier with three mana untapped and a Vampire in hand, where every cheap cast is now a burn spell aimed at the whole table. Or Edgar on the battlefield, median turn six and 52.2% by turn six, handing the board first strike, haste and a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire at declare, with Akroma's Will available to add flying and double strike, or indestructible and protection from each colour, or both.

When you take it, take it insured. A protection piece is held in 68.0% of games and 56.6% by turn six, and four of the nine are board-wide. Teferi's Protection answers the sweeper and the counterattack with one card. Commit on the turn you can cover, and the table gets exactly one window to stop you — usually holding the wrong card for the job.
matchups:
VS SWEEPER CONTROL: The wrath is a worse card against you than it is against anyone else at the table, and you should build the whole matchup on that. The machine is not made of creatures — Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Caretaker's Talent, Patchwork Banner, Legion's Landing and Elspeth, Storm Slayer all survive, Purphoros is indestructible, and eminence rebuilds at one token per Vampire cast with nothing spent. So commit exactly the width that converts now and keep the next multiplier in hand: "commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further" and "buy resilience instead of restraint" (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). With a payoff down you do not need seven bodies to matter — stack 008 puts one two-mana Vampire at 10 damage to each opponent through two doublers. Rebuild worst-first afterwards. Assume the white or blue seat sitting on four or more untapped mana with no play is representing the sweeper, and time your commitment to a protection piece: held in 68.0% of games, 56.6% by turn six, four of nine board-wide, with Teferi's Protection covering the wrath and the swing-back together. Impact Tremors is the card that flips this matchup — two mana, invisible, and it turns every rebuild into damage the sweeper cannot undo.

VS STAX AND TAX: Structurally your best matchup, and the reason is a rules detail worth knowing cold. Eminence is a triggered ability that functions from the command zone, not a cast, so a Sphere effect taxes the Vampire spell and never touches the token it makes. The curve cooperates: 9 one-drops and 17 two-drops out of 63 spells. You are the beatdown here by force, racing the lock's completion, so recount your hand under the tax and name your outs early — the piece that beats you is the one that stops tokens entering or taxes creature spells, not the flashiest lock piece (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Herald's Horn rebates {1} on every Vampire creature spell and Patchwork Banner taps for any colour while pumping the type, which is a real counter-tax on a deck built to cast two spells a turn. Edgar himself is the first thing a tax prices out at six mana, and you do not need him: median cast turn six, 52.2% by turn six, and the token engine has been running since turn one regardless. Leave him zoned longest in this matchup, aim Despark at the tax rather than the trophy, and remember Ancient Tomb is two mana under any Sphere.

VS AGGRO AND CREATURE MIRRORS: Re-ask the role and take the other seat (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Against a faster board you are the control, and this deck can do that without changing a single card — lifelink tokens from Charismatic Conqueror, Legion's Landing, Mavren Fein and Preacher of the Schism, deathtouch from Preacher and Vampire of the Dire Moon and the Conqueror, first strike from Edgar, Cemetery Gatekeeper and everything Stromkirk Captain touches. A wide board turns their small creatures into dead cards without you drawing anything, and that virtual advantage triples against three opponents (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). Charismatic Conqueror is the card that flips it: every artifact or creature entering untapped under any opponent either comes in tapped or hands you a lifelink Vampire, and with a payoff down that token deals damage to all three seats on their turn. Olivia's Wrath is your asymmetric answer — each non-Vampire creature gets -X/-X for the Vampires you control, and the goldfish has you at 4.12 bodies by turn six. Toxic Deluge kills your own board, so hold it only for a board you genuinely cannot race. Spend life freely where it buys tempo — Ancient Tomb, Mana Confluence, Caves of Koilos and four fetches are all charging you — but track each opponent's clock separately, because 40 life attacked from three directions is not 40 life.

VS COMBO: You are the clock and you are fast enough to be one. The lord package assembles at a mean turn of 2.58 and the token-to-damage payoff at 3.45, which is ahead of most combo decks' assembly. Present the plan that survives being answered: an interrupted multiplier costs one card, an interrupted alpha strike costs the board, so lead with entry damage rather than a swing (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Held answers rot against combo, and the last profitable moment is now — spend Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile and Despark on the piece that ends the game rather than saving them for the piece that looks scary (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). This is the matchup where casting Edgar early for reasons other than combat is right: he switches on Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat for free. Do not steer toward the Conqueror loop here — it is drawn in 4.8% of games, and both stacks 004 and 006 break it to one instant-speed removal spell at any iteration. Race, and let the loop happen to you if it happens at all.

VS GRAVEYARD HATE: This one is close to free, and you should encourage it. There is no graveyard plan to attack — the kills are token entries, attack triggers and a lifegain loop, and every payoff is a permanent on the battlefield. A Rest in Peace effect costs the reanimator seat their deck and costs you one trigger on Cemetery Gatekeeper, whose enters ability needs a card in a graveyard to exile before its damage trigger can ever check. Say yes to that trade every time and help the hate resolve. Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet is your own flip card against a recursion deck: opponents' nontoken creatures get exiled instead of dying and you get a 2/2 Zombie for each, which is hate stapled to a body a lord already pumps. Cemetery Gatekeeper is the second, and it is a first-striking Vampire on the way to being incidental hate.
